subject: Post-call: DataForge initial eval and operational tooling test plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap and proposed next tests

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful clarity on the DataForge inference needs. Short recap and the test plan I promised. Please skim and tell me which items you want prioritized this week.

Recap (high level)
- Workload: multi-tenant inference for a real-time user-facing feature (average response 90-120 tokens, peak concurrency ~600-1,000 sessions).
- SLOs: p50 ~100ms, p95 <250ms, p99 target <500ms for most requests.
- Cost target: lower than current self-hosted GPU cost by at least 25% per 1M tokens.
- Security: SOC2 evidence requested, VPC peering for production, long-term audit logs.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model traces, request-level metadata (user id, request id, model variant), exports to Datadog.

Proposed short test plan (48-72h canonical tests)
1) Throughput and latency sweep
   - Run a stepped load from 100->1,000 concurrent sessions using your average prompt mix (90-120 tokens). Measure p50/p95/p99 for Redwood hosted, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex (we can provide runbooks and synthetic harness).
2) Traceability and dashboards
   - Send requests with a tracing header (x-df-trace-id) and validate end-to-end visibility in Datadog and in our per-route dashboard. Confirm token-level breakdown and top-k cost contributors.
3) Fallback/resilience flow
   - Simulate model OOM and test automatic fallback to a quantized variant; verify no hard errors to users and measure latency impact.
4) Cost delta calculation
   - Run 100k tokens through each platform using the exact prompt set and compute normalized cost per 1M tokens with the same GPU equivalent.
5) Security/compliance check (light)
   - Exchange SOC2 summary and confirm VPC peering timelines.

What we will provide
- A small harness and prompts to reproduce your prompt mix.
- A one-page observability spec and dashboard links.
- A mutual action plan template (attached).

Ask for DataForge
- Confirm which of the above tests you want first and whether you want Redwood to run comparative jobs on your behalf or run them within your environment.
- Share a short sample prompt set (10-20 representative requests) and a Datadog workspace id for dashboard verification.

I attached a 1-pager on our observability features and a mutual action plan with proposed milestones.

Next up: if you confirm, we will kickoff a 48h comparison run and follow up with a results deck.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0187
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@dataforge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean O'Connor <sean@edgecloud.io>
Date: 2026-02-11T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed next tests

Thanks Priyom — that looks like the right scope. A few clarifying items before we lock the run order:

1) For the hyperscaler comparisons, can you include the exact model variants you plan to test (eg. gpt-4o-like vs 7B quantized)? We want apples-to-apples as much as possible.
2) Tracing: we use Datadog tracing currently and will provide an API key or workspace id; can you also show an example span schema we should expect?
3) Data residency: production must stay in us-west-2, can the hosted test be pinned to that region?
4) Security: we will need SOC2 Type II PDF and a brief on retention windows for request logs.

Also, curious about two differentiators you mentioned: automatic prefix/KV caching and fallback model routing. For our service, cache hit rate will materially change cost — can you instrument cache-hit metrics in the run?

If ok, prioritize the throughput sweep and the tracing/dashboard verification first. Happy to share a 20-sample prompt set by EOD.

Regards,
Alex Nguyen
Head of ML Engineering, DataForge
alex@dataforge.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T20:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: DataForge next-tests and who owns what

Marissa / Rafael — quick internal coordination after Alex's note. He wants throughput sweep and tracing/dashboard verification prioritized and will provide sample prompts tonight. Key asks and suggested owners: 

- Model mapping and exact variants for comparison (Redwood vs Bedrock vs Vertex): Rafael to own. Please propose the closest equivalent open models and quantized variants; include tokenization differences. Target: deliver model mapping by EOD tomorrow.
- Test harness and scripts: Marissa to own. Use our load generator (k6 + custom harness) and ensure we can pin hosted region to us-west-2. Deliver CUE/test plan and runner commands.
- Observability instrumentation: Rafael + infra to confirm span schema and Datadog export. We need to ensure we capture: request_id, user_id, model_variant, cache_hit, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate. Rafael — include how to surface cache-hit % in per-route dashboard.
- Cost calc and results deck: I'll take the first pass on the cost normalization logic; will need raw token/time logs.

Risks/questions:
- If Bedrock/Vertex test variants are not directly comparable, call out assumptions explicitly.
- We may need a short ask to their infra team to allow synthetic load from their VPC if they want the run inside their account.

Deliverables timeline proposal:
- Model mapping: 2026-02-12 18:00 PST
- Harness & runner: 2026-02-13 12:00 PST
- 48h run (if agreed) starting 2026-02-14

Assigning: Rafael please confirm he can own model mapping and the observability span schema. Marissa please confirm you can produce runner scripts and the runbook for Alex.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed next tests

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for prioritizing throughput + tracing. Next concrete items and shared artifacts:

1) Attached: redwood-observability-1pager.pdf and a mutual action plan spreadsheet.
2) Model mapping: Rafael will send a mapping table tomorrow with the closest equivalent variants for Bedrock and Vertex plus quantized options.
3) Tracing/span schema: we will emit Datadog-compatible spans with the following minimal fields: trace_id, span_id, parent_id, timestamp_ms, request_id, user_id, model_variant, cache_hit, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate. We will share an example JSON span and a short ingestion guide.
4) Region: we can pin hosted runs to us-west-2 for parity.

Two quick asks from your side to unblock the early run:
- Share the 20-sample prompt set (you mentioned EOD) and a Datadog workspace id for verification.
- Confirm whether you want us to run comparative tests from Redwood-hosted infrastructure or within your account (we can do both; running within your account will require temporary access or runner instructions).

HubSpot link to this opportunity and the plan: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/DF-2026-001
Drive folder with attachments and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-dataforge-testplan

If you confirm the sample prompts and Datadog id, we will schedule the throughput sweep for Monday and send a short results deck within 48 hours of the run finishing.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-observability-1pager.pdf, dataforge-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
